thread.title: Tech Today: Western Dig LBO? Snap Slapped, More iPhone X Worries

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Western Dig LBO? Snap Slapped, More iPhone X Worries
text:
Here are some things going on today in your world of tech:
Snap slapped
Shares of Snap ( SNAP ) are down $1.10, or 5.5%, at $19.33, after Citigroup 's Mark May cut his rating on the shares to Sell from Neutral, and cut his price target to $14 from $18, citing a sharp rise in negative reviews for its Snapchat application following a recent redesign of the app, according to a summary of the report provided by TheFlyontheWall .
As the Qualcomm turns
Shares of Qualcomm ( QCOM ) are down $1.85, or almost 3%, at $63, in early trading, and Broadcom ( AVGO ) is off 2 cents at $248.87, amidst the latest jousting in their M&A battle. Qualcomm will increase its purchase price for NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) to $127.50 from $110.
Broadcom, fresh from a partial endorsement from International Shareholder Services , slammed Qualcomm's raised bid , accusing the Qualcomm board of neglecting its fiduciary duty.
The next step is Qualcomm’s March 6th shareholder meeting.
Vijay Rakesh with Mizuho and Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein are among those commenting this morning .
More weak iPhone X chatter
Shares of Apple ( AAPL ) are are up 37 cents at $171.96, as the chatter continues about weaker-than-expeced sales of its iPhone X . The latest bit comes from the Nikkei Asian Review ’s Kenichi Yamada , who writes that Samsung Electronics (005930KS), Apple’s supplier for the organic light-emitting diode , or OLED, panels on the phone, has cut its plans for production for iPhone X by “around 60%,” producing enough for perhaps "20 million or fewer iPhone X,” without citing any sources.
Raising Universal Display
That Samsung rumor, if true, would not be great for Universal Display ( OLED ), a supplier to Samsung materials used in OLED. However, Needham & Co .’s James Ricchiuti raised his rating on shares of Universal to Buy from Hold, writing that he’s been “trying to thread the needle on OLED since last summer,” and “looking for the right entry point."
He’s convinced that’s now, as the stock heads for its earnings report this Thursday , after market close.
“Expectations are “clearly more cautious than prior quarters,” there are more positives than negatives after Universal last week renewed its contract with Samsung .
Universal shares are up 10 cents at $155.05.
A Western Dig LBO?
Talk of leveraged buyouts is an increasing approach by analysts to stock prices they don’t like.
Following a note last week from Credit Suisse suggesting that Lam Research ( LRCX ) could be LBO’d, today comes a note from RBC Capital ’s Amit Daryanani stating that "We think Western Digital ( WDC ) could be an attractive LBO candidate, especially given multiple PE firms that were involved in the Toshiba asset sale,” referring to December’s resolution between Western and Toshiba ( 6502JP ) to allow a consortium led by Bain Capital to buy the NAND chip manufacturing unit of Toshiba.
Daryanani, who has an Outperform rating on Western, and a $115 price target, notes that in the "recent market selloff,” given "WDC under-performance (vs. S&P500 and STX),” Western stock is "at ~6x EV/FCF (fourth cheapest in S&P500)."
He also observes that there is a "large group of interested buyers in NAND given high interest in Toshiba from PE, OEMs, China Inc, etc."
Daryanani suggests a $105 takeout price for Western.
Western stock is down 87 cents, or 1%, at $84.04 in early trading.
Raising numbers for Salesforce, Hewlett
Shares of cloud computing pioneers Salesforce ( CRM ) and Workday ( WDAY ) both get some good news from Deutsche Bank ’s Karl Keirstead raised his price targets for both, to $130 from $120 for Salesforce, and $115 form $105 for Workday, in advance of both companies’ earnings reports next week.
Keirstead cites positive channel checks, though he has Salesforce at Buy but Workday at Hold, citing high expectations for Workday in advance of the report.
Salesforce is down 36 cents at $112.50, and Workday is up 76 cents at $124.77.
Another stock getting a boost in advance of earnings is Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ), which got an upgrade by Loop Capital ’s Anandah Baruah to Buy from Hold, in advance of its report, also after market on Thursday. Baruah sees “multiple catalysts” in the next year for Hewlett, including expense cuts and the completion of its current buyback program.
Hewlett stock is up 4 cents at $16.43.
And shares of Veritone ( VERI ), which uses artificial intelligence approaches to analyze various kinds of content, are unchanged as Darren Aftahi with Roth Capital slashed his price target to $32 from $62 on the stock in advance of its report on February 26th. Aftahi maintains a Buy rating, but writes that he has decided to take a more “conservative” approach to valuation, according to a summary of the note from TheFlyontheWall .
